## Episode Thesis

Erik Selin is interviewed on the day of a stock-market listing for a small aerospace and defence group that he and Martin Nobel own almost 75% of. The group was built from three acquired companies: Turntime, Slingspray and Pentaxia. Selin describes the group as profitable, cash-generative and built on long customer relationships in defence and aircraft programmes, and he plans more add-on acquisitions. Most of the rest of the episode covers the proposed Swedish billionaire tax, which Selin criticises, and possible Swedish government coalitions; no explicit buy or sell calls are made.
